correctness.rationale: Graph union is Cartesian product and graph join is the convex free sum at the origin. Cone-volume scaling yields Beta radial variables and Dirichlet(a,b,1) gauges, proving all-degree rising-factorial moments and the factorial volume recursion. For normalized pair moments, unions preserve internal ratios while cross-union ratios are 1; at joins cross ratios are (n+1)/(n+2) and internal ratios are multiplied by [(a+2)/(a+1)][(n+1)/(n+2)]. Induction proves the sharp edge upper bound and all nonedge signs. Weighted exact integration of the P4 stable-set polytope gives -11/3750 for its nonadjacent endpoints, and induced-P4 exclusion gives the hereditary converse. Independent exact-rational simplex integrations corroborated 564 graphs, 1120 cubic moments, and the P4 boundary; finite checks do not prove the infinite claim.

The graph decomposition alone does not imply continuous-volume moment identities without the free-sum Dirichlet integration. The earlier complete multipartite family is strictly contained in cographs, and the new hereditary P4 sign boundary is not entailed by its within/between-part formulas.

value.rationale: The theorem gives exact integration for every polynomial observable on an infinite graph class via the cotree, a sharp quantitative negative-dependence bound, an exact positive/zero/negative covariance partition recovering the graph, and a maximal-hereditary boundary witnessed by an analytically computed P4 nonedge correlation. Alternating cotrees extend well beyond complete multipartite and rooted-forest-comparability special cases. These are structural, motivated polytope-geometric facts, not isolated small computations.
